statement.p: On a piece of paper, draw the graph of a continuous function y=f(x) that satisfies the following three conditions. f'(x) \lt 0\quad\mbox{for}\quad x \lt -2, f'(x) > 0\quad\mbox{for}\quad -2 \lt x \lt 2, f'(x) > 0\quad\mbox{for}\quad 2 \lt x

Approximate your function by picking a segment from the following for each of the sections of your graph, first for x \lt -2, then for -2 \lt x \lt 2, and then for 2 \lt x. (You should, of course, imagine sliding the pieces vertically up or down to make the function you create be continuous.)

image.shortdescription: a line decreasing from top left to bottom right of the graph
a line increasing from bottom left to top right of the graph
a curve increasing with decreasing slope from bottom left to top right of the graph
a horizontal line through the center of the graph
a curve decreasing with increasing slope from top left to bottom right of the graph
a curve decreasing with decreasing slope from top left to bottom right of the graph
a curve which starts at the top left, decreases for a bit and then increases to the top right
a curve increasing with increasing slope from bottom left to top right of the graph
a curve which starts at zero, increases to a peak and then decreases back to zero

solution.p: Because f'(x) \lt 0 for x \lt -2, the first segment must be one of 1, 5, or 6. Similarly, because f'(x) > 0 for -2 \lt x \lt 2, the second segment must be one of 2, 3, or 8. And lastly, the third segment must be 2, 3, or 8.
